purpose: Short-lived, pinned fallback for the first cycle only when the deterministic research queue is unavailable. This ordering is not a research ranking.

candidates.title: The Hadwiger-Nelson Problem
candidates.statement: What is the minimum number of colors needed to color the points of the plane such that no two points at distance 1 have the same color?
candidates.bounded_target: Reproduce one published 4-uncolorability certificate for a pinned finite unit-distance graph, then isolate one explicit forced-coloring implication that can seed a reduction search.
theory_starting_points: Translate 4-colorability into a symmetry-broken SAT model and map proof clauses back to forced-coloring implications.
Treat a checked unsatisfiable core as a hypergraph and look for a human-auditable forcing chain or removable vertex orbit.
falsification_targets: Search for any edge whose pinned coordinates are not at unit distance under exact arithmetic.
Build an independent coloring encoding and search for a valid 4-coloring of the claimed certificate graph.
Check whether symmetry-breaking clauses accidentally remove legitimate colorings.
candidates.baseline_verification: Verify the pinned graph, CNF mapping, and published proof/checker path before treating any reduced core or forcing implication as evidence.
candidates.novelty_boundary: Reproducing the published lower-bound certificate is baseline verification, not novel progress on the parent problem. Any newly reduced core or forcing lemma remains unverified until independently checked and human reviewed.
